analysis.title: GS Wilson - weekly mash 2 Oct 2026
key_insights: Rates-led pain continues, but the week brought marginal shifts: quarter-end rebalancing flows, soft core PCE, more nuanced Fed speakers on near-term hikes, and jobs data with no wage pressure. GS pushed out its forecast for an October Fed hike.
US 10y and 30y yields look like they may have marked near-term exhaustion on the day before the note (Thursday).

A disorderly European rates move is seen as more concerning than the US one. EU decision-making is more complex, monetary policy has limited room for accommodation, French elections are due next year, and political leadership is less clear than in past stress episodes.
GS rule of thumb: equities can absorb a rates move until it reaches 2 standard deviations in a month. That threshold was basically hit this week.
Rates stress is spilling into credit. HY had its largest 1-day decline in 18 months last week, and credit vol moved by a good size this week.
Higher yields force governments to recalibrate fiscal plans, with fiscal discipline imposed, and leave central banks with less to do as financial conditions tighten sharply.

Positioning is already light. Global long/short hedge fund net exposure is in the 5th percentile on a 1-year lookback, 7th on 3-year and 9th on 5-year. US equity exposure alone is at 0%-2% on those measures.

After 2 days in Riyadh, Wilson sees the catalyst calendar into US mid-terms and Israeli elections as opening the possibility of a change in trajectory of the Middle East conflict. Reported oil flows have regained pre-March levels.
Meta stock rose 30% in September. The Muse launch and consumer AI use cases (Instinct and others) are accelerating AI adoption.
The America.gov AI launch could change the commonly perceived AI narrative on utility, productivity and application.

Micron results were good enough to hold the share price near record highs. META's September move plus early Q4 new highs in Nvidia and Nasdaq point to a broadening from capex beneficiaries to AI facilitators.
Wilson expects narrow breadth to be a feature of the next significant move higher in equities. GS added AMZN to its Conviction list earlier this week.

Wilson argues 'demographics, multiplied by effective agentic deployment, are destiny'. With social unrest in Europe, higher yields and superintelligence discussions at the White House, he finds it hard to resist US tech over other geographies.
